_comment: What the installed app reads to find out whether it is out of date.
TO PUBLISH A RELEASE: bump `version` and `build`, then set `url`, `bytes`
and `sha256` on each platform. The checksums are not optional and must not
be guessed — the app refuses to hand a downloaded installer to the OS
unless its bytes hash to the value here, which is the only thing standing
between a corrupted or substituted download and an executable the reader
runs with their own privileges. Take them from the release itself:
gh release view v<VERSION> --repo SpencerSmithSite/council \
--json assets --jq '.assets[] | "\(.name) \(.size) \(.digest)"'
This file and assets/js/download.js state the same versions, URLs and
sha256 checksums, so `node scripts/check-council-release.mjs` from the
repo root proves they agree. Run it after editing either one; a mismatch
means either the page offers a build the app will not update to, or the
reverse.
Linux also has a `deb` object (url, bytes, sha256) for the Debian package
the download page offers beside the AppImage. The installed app only reads
kind, url, bytes, sha256, version and build on a platform, and ignores
every other key, so `deb` does not change what an update installs.
Served from the site rather than the GitHub releases API because app
releases here are marked pre-release (the corpus releases are what
`releases/latest` points at), so there is no stable `latest` URL for the
app to follow — and because a static file on the site is one request with
no rate limit.
notes: Seven branches of the church in one library of 734 sources, a Stop button that stops, and search that keeps Greek and accented names. Downloaded collections need downloading again once.
